messages.subject: maps don't match
parts:
Hello,

I've never used R before, so pardon me if this is a silly question. I have two sets of individuals from a cross, one of which was chosen for genotyping randomly and the other half of which was chosen based on phenotype.  The random individuals are meant to be used for estimating the genetic map and the effect sizes of the QTLs.  All of the individuals are meant to be used for mapping. 

I made a genetic map using the random individuals - using ripple to establish marker order and then est.map.  I changed the marker order in the whole dataset using switch.order (it worked) and then tried to use replace.map to take the map generated from the random individuals and put it into the whole dataset. What is odd is that without any errors or changes the map for the whole dataset is a different length than the map generated from the random dataset, despite the fact that they should be the same thing.

Does anybody have any idea why this might be?  Is the program working in some way I am not aware of to produce this result?  Am I missing a step?  I apologize if this isn't enough information.

If you have any insight, thank you!!

CY

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] maps don't match
parts:
Could you post a portion of your code?

All I can think is that, in using replace.map(), you didn't assign the result back to the cross object. If you typed

replace.map(mycross, newmap)

then nothing would actually happen (though a summary of the cross should print). You need to do

mycross <- replace.map(mycross, newmap)

karl

From your code below, it should be that the malpal dataset is unchanged, but you'll have created a new dataset 'malpal_newmap' that is the same as malpal but contains the new map.

karl

> This is the record of code I've been keeping:
>
>
>
> malpal<-switch.order(malpal, 3, c("marker", "marker", etc)
>
>
> Then I reestimated the map for the random data set liked this:
>
>
> random_alt_map <- est.map(random_alt, 3, error.prob=.01)
>
>
> Replaced it in the original dataset like this:
>
> random_alt<-replace.map(random_alt, random_alt_map)
>
>
> And replaced it into the malpal dataset:
>
>
> malpal_newmap<-replace.map(malpal, random_alt_map)

>
